meal.title: Understanding the generated main.c file
meal.objective: Identify the default structure of the main.c file created by the IDE

voice.script: What does the blank file that Code::Blocks creates actually contain? When you start a new console project the IDE drops a starter file named main dot c. Here is the generated file: it begins with a line that starts with hash include, which tells the compiler to pull in a library of standard definitions. Below that you see the main function, the entry point where the operating system hands control to your program. The main function returns an integer value to indicate how the program finished. That's the whole default skeleton you get every time. Try creating a new project and locate the #include line and main function in the file.
